If you're willing to wait a little while rather than rushing to buy the latest Apple product on launch day, Apple's refurbished product store has always been a solid option. Generally speaking, you'll need to wait around three months after a new product launches before the first refurbished models appear on Apple's official website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but note that they use different quality standards and warranty policies…

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished store gets you roughly a 15% discount, but the product is essentially indistinguishable from brand new. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • A brand-new outer shell, so absolutely no scratches or wear
  • A brand-new battery with the same battery life as a new product
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Eligible for Apple's standard one-year warranty, identical to new products
  • Also eligible for AppleCare+ coverage

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box instead of the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed's pricing can be more competitive, but note that the protection you get on the condition of the item is not the same as Apple's:

  • Inspection and testing performed by the seller, not Apple
  • Used outer shell, so there will be scratches and wear (see below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to retain at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be genuine Apple
  • Amazon offers a 90-day warranty rather than Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and wear, Amazon offers three grades of quality classification:

  • Premium / Excellent: no visible surface wear when inspected from 12 inches away
  • Good: light scratches, barely visible when held at arm's length from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: scratches easily visible and palpable

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is much vaguer than Amazon about what your money gets you:

  • No commitment on cosmetic condition, only promises 'like-new performance and reliability'
  • Beyond the above, no battery condition details are provided
  • No information provided on accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company's definitions for each tier are not clear.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product in the same condition and with the same Apple warranty as a brand-new item, Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

That said, Amazon Renewed's pricing can be considerably lower, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs listed above, it's a decent option too. Especially if, as we suggest, you're looking to save money by upgrading to the iPhone 17 Pro rather than the latest model this year (since the only thing you'd be giving up is a cable), there are some genuinely attractive deals:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange for $1,214 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Deep Blue for $1,215 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Silver for $1,208 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange for $1,164 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Deep Blue for $1,170 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Silver for $1,171 (originally $1,299 new) — just $1 off the all-time low

As for Walmart Restored, I'd be concerned that their promises are too vague, but if you're not happy you can always return it.
